workload.problem: damped harmonic oscillator x'' + 2 zeta omega x' + omega^2 x = 0, classical RK4, fixed step (perf_card.py)

arm_labels.eagle_term8: eagle host, termination loop, up to 8 threads
arm_labels.eagle_compact8: eagle host, termination + compaction, up to 8 threads
arm_labels.eagle_reorder8: eagle host, termination + compaction + reorder, up to 8 threads
arm_labels.eagle_reorder1: eagle host, termination + compaction + reorder, 1 thread

arms.eagle_term8: The GPU card's eagle graph arm, unchanged, on the host: the same hawk step kernel, eagle.deploy and eagle.until_done call, run by eagle's OpenMP host team; one code base for GPUs and CPUs. On this card: spread S=100, N=1,000,000: 34.6 ms; spread S=1000, N=1,000,000: 330 ms; uniform S=1000, N=1,000,000: 648 ms. Fastest in 7 of 12 cells.
arms.eagle_term1: The same loop on one thread: the difference to the 8-thread row is the threading alone. On this card: spread S=100, N=1,000,000: 275 ms (7.96× eagle 8-thread time); spread S=1000, N=1,000,000: 2.64 s (7.98× eagle 8-thread time); uniform S=1000, N=1,000,000: 5.17 s (7.98× eagle 8-thread time). Fastest in 0 of 12 cells.
arms.eagle_compact8: The GPU card's compaction arm on the host: the launch covers only the samples still running, the map rebuilt every 16 steps when a sample finished. On this card: spread S=100, N=1,000,000: 52.1 ms (1.51× eagle 8-thread time); spread S=1000, N=1,000,000: 301 ms (0.91× eagle 8-thread time); uniform S=1000, N=1,000,000: 957 ms (1.48× eagle 8-thread time). Fastest in 1 of 12 cells.
arms.eagle_compact1: The compaction loop on one thread: the difference to the 8-thread row is the threading alone. On this card: spread S=100, N=1,000,000: 208 ms (6.02× eagle 8-thread time); spread S=1000, N=1,000,000: 1.76 s (5.32× eagle 8-thread time); uniform S=1000, N=1,000,000: 7.25 s (11.2× eagle 8-thread time). Fastest in 0 of 12 cells.
arms.eagle_reorder8: The GPU card's reorder arm on the host: the live samples moved to the front of every plane when they spread thin, restored to sample order at the end (inside the wall). On this card: spread S=100, N=1,000,000: 131 ms (3.79× eagle 8-thread time); spread S=1000, N=1,000,000: 397 ms (1.2× eagle 8-thread time); uniform S=1000, N=1,000,000: 953 ms (1.47× eagle 8-thread time). Fastest in 0 of 12 cells.
arms.eagle_reorder1: The reorder loop on one thread: the difference to the 8-thread row is the threading alone. On this card: spread S=100, N=1,000,000: 274 ms (7.92× eagle 8-thread time); spread S=1000, N=1,000,000: 1.72 s (5.2× eagle 8-thread time); uniform S=1000, N=1,000,000: 7.26 s (11.2× eagle 8-thread time). Fastest in 0 of 12 cells.
arms.numba_prange: Compiles a plain Python loop to machine code with no separate language; each sample keeps its state in registers across all of its steps and stops on its own, so finished samples cost nothing. On this card: spread S=100, N=1,000,000: 39 ms (1.13× eagle 8-thread time); spread S=1000, N=1,000,000: 388 ms (1.17× eagle 8-thread time); uniform S=1000, N=1,000,000: 1.8 s (2.78× eagle 8-thread time). Fastest in 1 of 12 cells.
arms.jax_shard8: The JAX arm spread over 8 CPU devices: the batch is sharded and each shard runs its own vmapped while loop, with no cross-shard step synchronisation. On this card: spread S=100, N=1,000,000: 42.6 ms (1.23× eagle 8-thread time); spread S=1000, N=1,000,000: 410 ms (1.24× eagle 8-thread time); uniform S=1000, N=1,000,000: 411 ms (0.635× eagle 8-thread time). Fastest in 3 of 12 cells.
arms.jax_vmap: Compiles the whole loop once and batches a per-sample while loop with vmap; the same code runs on GPUs and differentiates with jax.grad. On this card: spread S=100, N=1,000,000: 185 ms (5.35× eagle 8-thread time); spread S=1000, N=1,000,000: 1.77 s (5.34× eagle 8-thread time); uniform S=1000, N=1,000,000: 1.76 s (2.72× eagle 8-thread time). Fastest in 0 of 12 cells.
arms.torch_masked: Runs the masked array version on a multi-threaded tensor library; it fits where the computation already lives next to a PyTorch model or needs autograd. On this card: spread S=100, N=1,000,000: 304 ms (8.79× eagle 8-thread time); spread S=1000, N=1,000,000: 3.02 s (9.15× eagle 8-thread time); uniform S=1000, N=1,000,000: 2.76 s (4.26× eagle 8-thread time). Fastest in 0 of 12 cells.
arms.numpy_masked: No compile step and no dependency beyond NumPy; masked array code computes every sample every step, so it fits dense batches where all samples run to the end (the uniform configuration). On this card: spread S=100, N=1,000,000: 1.59 s (46× eagle 8-thread time); spread S=1000, N=1,000,000: 16.4 s (49.5× eagle 8-thread time); uniform S=1000, N=1,000,000: 15.6 s (24× eagle 8-thread time). Fastest in 0 of 12 cells.
arms.mp_numpy: Spreads NumPy over processes with the standard library alone; each chunk stops once its own samples are done. On this card: spread S=100, N=1,000,000: 244 ms (7.05× eagle 8-thread time); spread S=1000, N=1,000,000: 2.22 s (6.72× eagle 8-thread time); uniform S=1000, N=1,000,000: 2.2 s (3.4× eagle 8-thread time). Fastest in 0 of 12 cells.
arms.python_loops: Nothing to install and each line can be stepped in a debugger; run only at small N here. On this card: spread S=100, N=10,000: 60.5 ms (158× eagle 8-thread time); spread S=1000, N=10,000: 580 ms (166× eagle 8-thread time); uniform S=1000, N=1,000: 266 ms (381× eagle 8-thread time). Fastest in 0 of 12 cells.
